observation_summary: SerializationUtils.clone() fails with a ClassNotFoundException when attempting to clone primitive classes (e.g., int.class) because the custom resolveClass method in ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream does not correctly handle primitive type resolution.
reasoning_summary: The issue is an incorrect implementation of the resolveClass method within the ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream. The current implementation attempts to resolve classes using specific class loaders but fails to account for primitive types, which are handled differently in Java's standard ObjectInputStream. The fix requires updating the procedural logic of the resolveClass method to include a fallback to the superclass implementation or a specific check for primitive types, which is a procedural/algorithmic correction rather than a missing guard or a simple value assignment.
evidence_used: Bug report description detailing the failure to resolve primitive classes
Stack trace showing ClassNotFoundException in SerializationUtils.clone

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding a check/fallback, the core issue is the incorrect procedural strategy for resolving classes, which is better classified as an algorithmic/methodological flaw in the custom class loader implementation.
The issue is not a mismatch in the interface contract between components, but rather an internal failure of the custom class loader to correctly implement the class resolution logic.
